title: Credential adapter answer
description: What a credential adapter prints on its standard output, once, as one JSON document. An adapter is a program of the machine's, started by the runner outside the enclosure, that knows one kind of host, a source code host say: it mints or fetches a token and says how the token is used, because hosts differ in that and the runner knows none of them. It exits 0 with this document, or not 0 with a line on standard error.

token.description: The token, for every apply entry that has none of its own.

expires_at.description: When the token stops working, RFC 3339. The runner asks again five minutes before. Absent means it does not expire.

apply.description: Where the token goes. Asked again, an adapter answers with the same hosts, schemes and paths: they are fixed when the run starts, and only the token changes.

scheme.description: bearer sets Authorization: Bearer and the token. basic sets Authorization: Basic with username and the token as the password. header sets the header named to the token. The set is closed: an adapter chooses among what the runner does.

paths.description: The paths of these hosts the run may ask for, the policy's path grammar; every other path of them is denied. Absent means every path.

placeholders.description: Variables the enclosure gets with a value that is no credential, for a program that does not start without one set: the proxy replaces what the program sends.
